With disruption well below 6, the occupation is resilient regardless of elasticity.
opus5_rationale: Core work is in-person, physically active, and relational — leading games, sports, aquatics, and community outings while motivating and physically assisting patients — none of which AI can perform. AI can meaningfully help only with peripheral tasks like documentation, progress tracking, treatment-plan drafting, and activity ideation, which is a modest share of the day. Elasticity is moderate: an aging population and mental health/addiction treatment create real latent demand, but reimbursement and funding constraints (especially in nursing homes) cap expansion regardless of productivity. With disruption well below the threshold, the occupation is resilient; AI becomes a documentation aid rather than a substitute.
openai_rationale: Recreational therapy involves a significant amount of physical interaction and personalized care, which limits AI's ability to disrupt core tasks. While AI can assist with administrative tasks like scheduling and documentation, the therapeutic activities themselves require human empathy and adaptability. Demand elasticity is moderate; while AI could make some aspects of therapy more efficient, the core demand is driven by human interaction and personalized care, which are not easily scalable. Thus, the occupation is resilient to AI disruption, with some potential for efficiency gains but no major shift in demand dynamics.
gpt55_rationale: Recreational therapy includes some cognitive and administrative work—assessment, treatment-plan design, documentation, and progress analysis—that AI can help streamline. However, the core job is hands-on, interpersonal, and safety-sensitive: motivating patients, leading activities, adapting in real time, assisting people with disabilities, and working in clinical or community settings. Demand could expand moderately if services became cheaper, especially for aging populations, mental health treatment, addiction recovery, and underserved care settings, but reimbursement, staffing models, and the need for in-person engagement limit explosive growth. Because AI is more likely to support planning and documentation than replace the embodied therapeutic role, the occupation is best classified as resilient.
gpt56sol_rationale: AI can assist with patient-record review, treatment-plan drafting, activity customization, progress analysis, and clinical documentation. However, the core work depends on in-person observation, motivation, empathy, real-time adaptation, group facilitation, and sometimes physical assistance, limiting automation. Lower costs could unlock meaningful demand among older adults and people with mental health or rehabilitation needs, although reimbursement, facility funding, and staffing constraints would limit expansion. Because AI primarily improves planning and administration rather than replacing direct therapeutic engagement, the occupation is resilient.
fable5_rationale: The core of recreational therapy is in-person, physically and emotionally engaged work — leading activities, motivating patients, providing hands-on assistance, and building therapeutic rapport — none of which AI can substitute for. AI meaningfully helps only with peripheral tasks like documentation, progress tracking, and treatment plan drafting. Elasticity is modest: an aging population creates some latent demand, but reimbursement and funding constraints in nursing homes and healthcare settings cap expansion regardless of cost. With disruption well below 7, the occupation is clearly resilient — AI streamlines admin work but leaves the therapeutic core intact.
grok45_rationale: Core work centers on in-person patient engagement through sports, games, community outings, arts, and adaptive activities that require physical presence, real-time motivation, empathy, and hands-on assistance—tasks AI cannot perform—while AI only assists peripheral elements like record review, plan drafting, and progress documentation. Demand is constrained by clinical need, insurance reimbursement, facility funding, and regulatory structures rather than pure price or speed, so even large productivity gains would unlock only limited additional volume among aging or mental-health populations. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI touches planning and admin but leaves the essential therapeutic interaction intact.

title: Registered nurses
claude_rationale: Nursing involves substantial physical presence, hands-on patient care, emotional support, and real-time clinical judgment that AI cannot replicate, though AI assists with documentation, monitoring, and some diagnostic support. Healthcare demand is highly elastic - an aging population, chronic disease management, and preference for home/community care create enormous latent demand that cheaper/faster healthcare delivery would unlock. However, the disruption score of 5 places this in the resilient category, as the core work remains fundamentally human-centered despite AI augmentation of peripheral tasks.
opus_rationale: Nursing involves substantial physical, hands-on patient care—lifting patients, administering treatments, monitoring equipment, providing emotional support—that AI cannot replace, though AI does meaningfully assist documentation, diagnostics, care planning, and patient education, placing disruption at moderate. Demand is structurally elastic given aging demographics, chronic disease prevalence, and persistent workforce shortages, so productivity gains would be absorbed by expanded care rather than headcount cuts. Because the core work remains anchored in human presence and physical caregiving with disruption at 4, the occupation is resilient; AI augments peripheral cognitive tasks but does not reshape the fundamental role.
opus5_rationale: Nursing is fundamentally hands-on: assessment, medication administration, patient handling, monitoring, and bedside comfort require physical presence and judgment in unpredictable settings, so core tasks remain outside AI's reach. AI will meaningfully reshape the documentation, charting, triage, care-plan drafting, and early-warning/monitoring layers — which consume a large share of a nurse's shift — pushing disruption to a moderate 4-5 rather than low. Demand elasticity is high because nursing care is chronically supply-constrained and rationed by staffing shortages and cost; freeing nurses from paperwork would be absorbed by more patient contact and expanded home/community care rather than headcount cuts. Since disruption stays at or below 6, the occupation is resilient: AI removes administrative burden and augments clinical vigilance without displacing the core role.
openai_rationale: Registered nurses perform a mix of physical and cognitive tasks, with a significant portion requiring direct patient interaction and care, which AI cannot fully replicate. AI can assist with administrative tasks, data management, and diagnostics, but the core nursing duties remain human-centric. Demand elasticity is moderate; while AI could make certain processes more efficient, the demand for nursing services is driven by demographic trends and healthcare needs, which are not easily expanded by cost reductions. Thus, the occupation is resilient to AI disruption, with technology augmenting rather than replacing human roles.
gpt55_rationale: AI will materially affect parts of registered nursing such as documentation, care-plan drafting, patient education, triage support, remote monitoring, and decision support. However, the core of the job still requires licensed in-person clinical judgment, medication administration, patient assessment, coordination with care teams, emotional support, and physical handling in unpredictable healthcare settings. Demand elasticity is moderate because aging, chronic disease, home health, and underserved care create latent demand, but utilization is constrained by reimbursement, staffing models, regulation, and the need for hands-on care. Because disruption remains moderate rather than high, the occupation is best categorized as resilient.
gpt56sol_rationale: AI will materially assist with documentation, patient monitoring, care-plan preparation, clinical decision support, and patient education. However, bedside assessment, medication administration, equipment operation, physical assistance, emotional support, and emergency response require licensed human presence in unpredictable settings. Lower-cost nursing services could unlock additional preventive, chronic, elder, and home-based care, although reimbursement, staffing ratios, facilities, and licensing constrain expansion. Because AI reshapes important cognitive and administrative tasks without replacing the occupation’s hands-on core, registered nursing remains resilient.
fable5_rationale: Nursing is the canonical moderate-disruption occupation: core work — administering medications, physical assessments, lifting and moving patients, operating equipment, providing emotional support — requires human presence, while AI meaningfully assists documentation, charting, care planning, patient monitoring alerts, and triage. Demand elasticity is moderate-to-high given an aging population, chronic disease burden, persistent nursing shortages, and latent demand for home-based and preventive care that cheaper coordination could unlock, though staffing budgets and reimbursement structures cap expansion. With disruption at 4, the net effect is resilient: AI will offload administrative burden and augment clinical decision-making, but the hands-on, empathetic core of nursing remains firmly human, and BLS already projects faster-than-average growth.
grok45_rationale: Core RN duties center on physical patient assessment, medication administration, equipment operation, hands-on monitoring, and in-person emotional support that require unpredictable real-world presence, so AI mainly assists peripheral knowledge tasks such as charting, data analysis, and care-plan suggestions rather than replacing the occupation’s essence. Demand elasticity is moderate because an aging population and rising chronic conditions already drive growth, and cheaper/faster nursing productivity would unlock more home care, preventive education, and access in underserved settings without fully saturating need. The combination keeps the occupation in the resilient category: AI changes workflows at the margins but does not fundamentally reshape or eliminate the need for human nurses.

title: Rehabilitation counselors
claude_rationale: Rehabilitation counseling involves substantial human-to-human interaction, empathy, and complex assessment of individual needs that require physical presence and emotional intelligence. While AI could assist with documentation, assessment tools, and resource matching, the core counseling relationship and personalized rehabilitation planning remain fundamentally human activities. Demand elasticity is high because cheaper, more accessible rehabilitation services could serve underserved populations and provide more intensive support, but the moderate disruption score keeps this in the resilient category rather than augment.
opus_rationale: The core work involves empathetic counseling, building trust, in-person assessment, advocacy, and physical resource coordination (e.g., locating wheelchairs)—all requiring human presence, compassion, and relationship-building that AI cannot replicate. AI can assist peripherally with documentation, resource matching, plan drafting, and progress tracking, but the central interpersonal counseling tasks remain human-driven, yielding a moderate disruption score. Demand is moderately elastic since cheaper administrative support could free counselors to serve more clients, but the work is heavily constrained by government budgets, regulatory licensure, and the fundamentally human caseload nature. With disruption at or below 6, the occupation is resilient: AI touches administrative edges but does not reshape the empathetic, presence-based core.
opus5_rationale: Core work is relational and empathetic — in-person counseling, building trust with clients who have disabilities, coordinating with employers, doctors, and community resources — which AI cannot substitute for. AI does meaningfully touch the substantial documentation, case-note, plan-drafting, resource-matching, and benefits/eligibility research portions of the job, freeing counselor time, so disruption is moderate rather than low. Elasticity is moderate: latent need is large (aging population, veterans, underserved disabled clients) but funding is dominated by constrained state and federal vocational rehabilitation budgets, capping headcount growth regardless of productivity. With disruption at 4, the occupation is resilient — AI reshapes paperwork and referral workflows at the periphery while the human counseling core remains.
openai_rationale: Rehabilitation counselors perform tasks that are predominantly interpersonal and require empathy, critical thinking, and direct client interaction, which are less susceptible to AI disruption. While AI can assist with administrative tasks and data management, the core counseling work remains human-centric. Demand elasticity is low due to regulatory and budgetary constraints, as well as the personal nature of the service, which limits the expansion of demand even if services become cheaper. Thus, the occupation is resilient to AI disruption, with AI augmenting rather than replacing core tasks.
gpt55_rationale: AI can materially assist rehabilitation counselors with intake summaries, documentation, benefits and resource navigation, vocational matching, progress tracking, and drafting rehabilitation plans. However, the core work depends on trust-based counseling, empathy, clinical judgment, advocacy, coordination with families and agencies, and adapting to clients’ disabilities and real-world constraints, so AI is more likely to support than replace the central relationship. Demand has some elasticity because disability, aging, veteran, and employment-support needs are substantial and often underserved, but public funding limits, licensing rules, and the need for human care constrain expansion. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to reshape the occupation’s core, the net effect is resilient.
gpt56sol_rationale: AI can substantially assist with assessments, rehabilitation-plan drafting, resource matching, documentation, progress monitoring, and routine client guidance. However, effective counseling still depends on human empathy, trust, nuanced observation, advocacy, and coordination across clients, families, employers, and healthcare professionals, often under licensing requirements. Demand has relatively high elasticity because disability and aging create substantial unmet need, although government budgets and reimbursement constraints will limit expansion. Because AI is likely to improve counselors’ capacity without fully reshaping the relationship-centered core, the occupation is resilient.
fable5_rationale: The core of rehabilitation counseling is empathetic, in-person relationship work with clients facing disabilities — counseling sessions, advocacy, and trust-building that resist automation, though AI can meaningfully assist with client assessments, rehabilitation plan drafting, resource matching, and case documentation. Elasticity is low-to-moderate: latent need among the aging population and people with disabilities exists, but demand is largely funded by constrained state budgets and mandated programs rather than price-sensitive consumers, so cheaper service delivery mostly relieves caseload backlogs rather than dramatically expanding headcount. With disruption well below 7, the occupation is resilient — AI streamlines the administrative periphery while the human counseling core remains intact.
grok45_rationale: Core duties center on interpersonal counseling, empathy-driven relationship building, in-person client evaluation, employer advocacy, and navigating complex real-world disability accommodations—tasks that require human presence and soft skills AI can only peripherally assist via documentation, resource search, or plan drafting. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper/faster service delivery would expand access for aging populations, veterans, and underserved clients currently limited by budgets, allowing more comprehensive support without fully offsetting productivity gains. Net effect is resilient as AI remains assistive rather than transformative to the occupation's relational core.

title: Respiratory therapists
claude_rationale: Respiratory therapy involves substantial hands-on patient care including physical assessments, chest physiotherapy, ventilator management, and direct patient interaction that requires human presence and clinical judgment. While AI may assist with diagnostic interpretation and treatment planning, the core work remains fundamentally physical and interpersonal. Demand elasticity is low because respiratory therapy needs are primarily driven by medical necessity rather than cost - patients with breathing disorders require treatment regardless of price, and regulatory/safety requirements limit how much care can be expanded even if costs decrease. The moderate disruption score combined with low elasticity keeps this occupation in the resilient category.
opus_rationale: Respiratory therapists perform hands-on physical work—administering treatments, operating ventilators, chest physiotherapy, drawing blood samples, and providing bedside patient care—that requires real-world physical presence and cannot be automated by AI. AI may assist peripherally with diagnostic test interpretation, monitoring data, and documentation, but the core therapeutic and patient-interaction tasks remain human-dependent. Demand is driven by aging demographics and respiratory disease prevalence rather than cost barriers, so productivity gains wouldn't dramatically expand consumption. With disruption well below 6, this occupation is resilient: AI touches the periphery (charting, analytics) but does not reshape the fundamentally physical, in-person nature of the work.
opus5_rationale: Core work is hands-on and physical: intubation support, ventilator setup and titration at bedside, chest physiotherapy, drawing arterial blood gases, and patient/family education in homes and ICUs. AI can improve ventilator weaning protocols, alarm triage, pulmonary function test interpretation, and documentation, but these are decision-support layers around an inherently in-person, licensed clinical role. Demand is highly elastic in the sense that aging demographics, COPD prevalence, and understaffed hospitals mean any efficiency gain gets absorbed by more patient coverage rather than headcount cuts. With disruption well below the threshold, this is clearly resilient — AI touches monitoring and charting but not the physical delivery of respiratory care.
openai_rationale: Respiratory therapists perform a mix of physical and cognitive tasks, including patient interaction, diagnostic testing, and treatment administration. While AI can assist with diagnostic tools and data analysis, the hands-on and interpersonal aspects of the job limit AI's disruption potential, resulting in a moderate disruption score. Demand elasticity is moderate; while AI could improve efficiency, the demand for respiratory therapists is driven by demographic trends and healthcare needs, which are not highly sensitive to cost reductions. Thus, the occupation is resilient, with AI augmenting rather than replacing core tasks.
gpt55_rationale: Respiratory therapy includes some cognitive and data-oriented tasks—interpreting pulmonary tests, monitoring ventilator settings, documenting progress, and educating patients—that AI decision support, remote monitoring, and automated charting can improve. However, the core work is still bedside and hands-on: assessing patients, managing equipment, responding in emergencies, performing airway clearance, and coordinating care in unpredictable clinical settings. Demand is moderately elastic because cheaper monitoring and workflow support could expand home care, outpatient management, and chronic respiratory disease services, but total need is still constrained by disease prevalence, staffing regulations, and clinical supervision requirements. Because disruption remains moderate rather than high, the occupation is best categorized as resilient.
gpt56sol_rationale: AI can improve documentation, interpret pulmonary tests, optimize ventilator settings, and flag changes in patient status, but respiratory therapy remains centered on bedside examination, equipment setup, airway treatment, emergency response, and patient instruction. Demand could expand moderately through greater access to outpatient monitoring, home care, and preventive management, especially as the population ages, although disease incidence, clinical regulation, and the need for in-person care limit expansion. Because AI primarily supports rather than replaces the occupation’s hands-on clinical core, respiratory therapists are likely to remain resilient.
fable5_rationale: Respiratory therapists perform hands-on bedside care—administering treatments, managing ventilators, chest physiotherapy, drawing blood, and physically monitoring critically ill patients—which requires physical presence and cannot be done by AI. AI will assist with peripheral tasks like documentation, ventilator setting optimization, and diagnostic interpretation, but the core work remains manual and clinical. Elasticity is moderate: demand is driven by demographics and disease prevalence (aging population, COPD) rather than cost, though cheaper monitoring could expand home-care and outpatient respiratory services somewhat. With low disruption, the occupation is clearly resilient, consistent with BLS's projected 12% growth.
grok45_rationale: Core duties center on hands-on patient examination, physical treatments such as chest physiotherapy, ventilator setup/monitoring in acute settings, and real-time clinical presence, so AI can only assist peripheral knowledge tasks like interpreting pulmonary function data, suggesting plans, or automating records. Demand is driven primarily by fixed demographic and disease prevalence factors (aging population, COPD, emergencies) with only moderate expansion possible via cheaper home care or outpatient access; productivity gains will not unlock unlimited new volume. title: Retail sales workers
claude_rationale: Retail sales work involves substantial physical presence, face-to-face customer interaction, and hands-on product demonstration that AI cannot replicate, though AI may assist with inventory management and basic product information. Demand for retail sales services is relatively inelastic - consumers don't dramatically increase shopping frequency or need more salespeople just because AI makes some aspects more efficient, and e-commerce already provides the cost-effective alternative that limits physical retail growth. The moderate disruption combined with low elasticity places this in the resilient category, as the core interpersonal and physical aspects of the work remain largely unchanged despite some AI-assisted tools.
opus_rationale: The core work is in-person customer interaction, physical product demonstration, stocking, and processing payments — tasks requiring real-world presence that AI cannot directly perform. AI affects the periphery (inventory systems, product recommendations, e-commerce competition that erodes foot traffic) but does not reshape the face-to-face selling core. Demand is also inelastic: cheaper retail labor does not unlock dramatically more in-store shopping, and the larger threat is e-commerce shifting volume away from physical stores rather than productivity-driven expansion. With disruption at or below 6, the occupation is resilient — AI touches the edges but the human-presence core remains intact, even if total headcount stays flat due to broader retail shifts.
opus5_rationale: Core work is in-person: greeting customers, physically showing and demonstrating merchandise, stocking, and processing payments on the floor — tasks AI cannot perform without embodiment. AI does touch the periphery meaningfully (product lookup, inventory and recommendation systems, self-checkout and clienteling apps), and e-commerce driven by AI recommendation engines diverts some transactions away from stores, but that is a channel-shift pressure rather than automation of the role itself. Elasticity is low-to-moderate: retail sales volume is bounded by consumer spending, so cheaper sales assistance does not create much new demand, though richer service could support more specialty and high-touch formats. With disruption at 4, the occupation lands in the resilient category — flat headcount with gradually shifting skill emphasis toward omnichannel and product expertise rather than large-scale displacement by AI.
openai_rationale: Retail sales work involves significant physical presence and interpersonal interaction, which limits the extent to which AI can disrupt core tasks. While AI can assist with inventory management and customer data analysis, the core tasks of engaging with customers and facilitating sales remain largely human-driven. Demand elasticity is low because the shift to online retail reduces the need for in-store sales staff, and the nature of retail work does not allow for a significant expansion in demand even if productivity increases. Thus, the occupation is resilient, with AI impacting peripheral tasks but not reshaping the core work.
gpt55_rationale: Retail sales work is partly in AI's path because product recommendations, basic customer questions, checkout, inventory lookup, promotions, and online sales support can be handled by chatbots, kiosks, self-checkout, and recommendation systems. However, much of the occupation still requires in-person presence, interpersonal persuasion, handling merchandise, stocking, monitoring the store environment, and assisting customers in unpredictable physical settings. Demand elasticity is low because cheaper sales assistance does not make consumers buy vastly more retail goods; spending is constrained by income, store traffic, and the shift toward e-commerce. The occupation is therefore best classified as resilient because AI will change many tools and workflows, but the core in-store service role is not fully automatable over the next decade.
gpt56sol_rationale: AI can automate product questions, recommendations, promotions, inventory lookup, and portions of checkout, while e-commerce and self-service systems reduce some routine customer interactions. However, much of the occupation still requires in-store presence, interpersonal persuasion, product demonstrations, loss awareness, stocking, and assistance with physical merchandise. Demand for retail goods is constrained by consumer income and underlying purchasing needs, so cheaper sales support is unlikely to generate enough additional purchases to offset major productivity gains. Because disruption remains moderate rather than high, the occupation is resilient under the specified thresholds, although routine positions are likely to face continued attrition.
fable5_rationale: The core of retail sales work requires physical presence in stores — greeting customers, demonstrating products, stocking shelves, and processing in-person transactions — which AI cannot directly perform, though AI-powered product recommendation, chatbots, and self-checkout erode the knowledge and transactional portions of the role. Elasticity is low because cheaper sales assistance does not meaningfully expand how much merchandise people buy in physical stores; the bigger structural pressure is e-commerce substitution, not AI-driven productivity absorption. Even if AI made each worker more efficient, retailers would trim headcount rather than expand service, but since disruption stays at moderate levels the occupation is resilient — pressured more by channel shift to online shopping than by AI reshaping the in-person work itself.
grok45_rationale: Core tasks mix physical presence (greeting, demonstrating products, stocking, handling merchandise and security) with language/cognitive elements (recommendations, explanations, answering questions, promotions), so AI tools already assist via POS systems, inventory software, and recommendation engines but cannot eliminate the need for in-store human interaction and unpredictable real-world presence. Elasticity is low because demand for physical retail assistance is constrained by store foot traffic, e-commerce substitution, and fixed consumer shopping patterns; productivity gains (self-checkout, AI kiosks) historically shrink headcount rather than unlock large latent demand for more sales help. With disruption only moderate, the occupation remains resilient overall even as tools change peripheral workflows.

title: Roofers
claude_rationale: Roofing is almost entirely physical work requiring manual dexterity, balance, and presence at unpredictable outdoor job sites - AI has minimal relevance to core tasks like installing shingles, measuring materials, or working at heights. Demand for roofing is relatively inelastic as it's driven by necessary building maintenance and construction rather than discretionary spending, with limited ability to expand significantly even if costs dropped. The occupation falls clearly into the resilient category due to very low disruption from AI technologies.
opus_rationale: Roofing is almost entirely physical, hands-on work performed outdoors at heights, involving climbing, lifting, cutting, and installing materials in unpredictable real-world conditions—tasks AI cannot perform. AI is irrelevant to the core work, touching only peripheral functions like estimating or material calculations. Demand is structurally tied to building stock and weather-driven repair needs and is not heavily suppressed by labor cost in a way that would explode with cheaper output. With disruption far below the threshold, this occupation is clearly resilient regardless of elasticity.
opus5_rationale: Roofing is almost entirely physical: climbing, lifting 60-pound bundles, cutting and fastening materials in unpredictable outdoor conditions at height — none of which AI can perform, and robotics for steep-slope roofs remains far from commercial viability. AI touches only peripheral tasks like drone-based roof inspection, measurement/estimating software, and scheduling or lead generation, which marginally speed up bidding but not the labor itself. Elasticity is low-to-moderate: roof replacement demand is driven by building stock, weather damage, and roof lifecycles rather than by service cost, though slightly cheaper estimating could pull some deferred repairs forward. With disruption near the floor, the occupation is clearly resilient — headcount is set by construction activity and labor supply, not AI capability.
openai_rationale: Roofing is a predominantly physical occupation requiring manual dexterity, physical strength, and the ability to work at heights, which makes it minimally susceptible to AI disruption. The core tasks involve hands-on installation and repair of roofing materials, which AI cannot perform. As for demand elasticity, the need for roofing services is relatively fixed and driven by construction and maintenance cycles rather than cost or speed. Even if AI could make some peripheral tasks more efficient, it would not significantly increase the demand for roofing services. Thus, the occupation is resilient to AI-driven changes.
gpt55_rationale: Roofing is overwhelmingly physical, on-site work involving climbing, lifting, removing materials, cutting, fastening, sealing, and handling varied roof conditions in unsafe and unpredictable environments. AI can help at the margins with drone inspections, measurement, estimating, scheduling, and customer quoting, but it does not materially automate the core installation and repair tasks over the next decade. Demand is relatively inelastic because roofs are replaced or repaired based on building stock, weather damage, age, and construction activity, though lower costs could modestly increase preventive maintenance or upgrades such as solar or green roofing. Because disruption to the core work is very low, the occupation is best categorized as resilient.
gpt56sol_rationale: Roofing is overwhelmingly physical, site-specific work requiring climbing, balance, dexterity, material handling, and adaptation to irregular structures and weather conditions. AI may improve estimates, measurements, inspections, scheduling, and safety monitoring, but practical robotics are unlikely to replace crews broadly within the next decade. Demand has low elasticity because roof installation and replacement are driven mainly by building construction, damage, and finite maintenance cycles rather than by the cost of roofer labor alone. The occupation is therefore resilient, with AI affecting peripheral planning and administrative tasks more than its hands-on core.
fable5_rationale: Roofing is almost entirely physical, hands-on work performed at heights in unpredictable outdoor conditions — removing old roofs, hauling 60-pound shingle bundles, cutting and installing materials — which AI cannot perform and near-term robotics cannot handle economically. AI's role is limited to peripheral tasks like drone-based measurement, estimating, and scheduling, which is why disruption is the explicit benchmark example of minimal (0-1). Elasticity is low because roof replacement demand is driven by weather damage, material lifespan, and construction cycles rather than labor cost; cheaper roofing wouldn't cause people to re-roof much more often. With disruption far below the threshold, the occupation is clearly resilient.
grok45_rationale: Core roofing tasks—climbing, lifting heavy materials, cutting and fastening shingles or membranes, working at heights outdoors—are almost entirely physical and site-specific, placing the occupation at the minimal end of the disruption scale; AI can at best assist with peripheral estimating, drone inspection, or material calculation. Demand is largely tied to the existing building stock, weather damage, and new construction volume rather than being heavily suppressed by price, so even large productivity gains would produce only modest expansion in total roofing work. Because disruption remains far below the threshold that reshapes daily tasks, the occupation is resilient: AI stays on the periphery and headcount continues to track construction and repair needs.

title: Sales engineers
claude_rationale: Sales engineers face high disruption as AI can assist with technical presentations, product customization analysis, proposal generation, and customer needs assessment - core knowledge work activities that comprise much of their role. However, the critical relationship-building, complex negotiation, and trust-establishment aspects still require human presence. Demand elasticity is moderate because while AI-enhanced sales processes could make technical sales more efficient and accessible to smaller companies, B2B technical sales are ultimately constrained by customer budgets and actual business needs rather than just cost of the sales process. The occupation will restructure as sales engineers who adapt to AI-augmented workflows thrive, while those who don't may be displaced by more tech-savvy competitors.
opus_rationale: Much of a sales engineer's work involves digital and cognitive tasks—preparing technical presentations, analyzing product fit, generating proposals, and providing troubleshooting support—all of which AI tools can meaningfully accelerate. However, the core of the role relies on relationship-building, trust, persuasion, in-person customer engagement, and bespoke needs assessment that resist automation, keeping disruption moderate rather than high. On elasticity, cheaper and faster technical sales support could expand the number of products and customers covered, but headcount is structurally tied to deal volume and human relationship management, capping expansion at moderate levels. Because disruption stays at 6 (AI augments the knowledge-work portions but does not reshape the human-centered core), the occupation is best classified as resilient.
opus5_rationale: Much of a sales engineer's work is knowledge-based and highly AI-assistable: building technical presentations, answering RFPs and security questionnaires, scoping requirements, configuring demos, and troubleshooting documentation. However, the core value lies in trust-building, in-person/live technical persuasion, and tailoring solutions in ambiguous enterprise negotiations, which keeps disruption at the lower end of 'high.' Elasticity is high because pre-sales technical support is currently rationed by cost — many mid-market and smaller deals never get an SE, and proliferation of increasingly complex technical products (including AI products themselves) expands the need for someone to translate technology into customer value. Productivity gains likely mean each SE covers far more accounts and more deals get technical coverage rather than headcount cuts, so the role is augmented with a shift toward higher-touch relationship and solution-architecture skills.
openai_rationale: Sales engineers engage in a mix of technical and interpersonal tasks, with AI likely enhancing their ability to analyze customer needs and tailor solutions. AI tools can assist in preparing presentations, analyzing customer data, and providing technical support, but the core task of building relationships and negotiating sales remains human-centric. The demand elasticity is high because as AI makes sales processes more efficient, the ability to handle more clients and offer more personalized solutions can significantly expand the market. Thus, while AI will disrupt the role, the increased demand for sophisticated products and services will likely absorb these productivity gains, leading to an 'augment' net effect.
gpt55_rationale: Sales engineers do a large amount of cognitive, language-based work that AI can materially assist: preparing technical presentations, drafting proposals, answering product questions, configuring solutions, summarizing customer requirements, and supporting troubleshooting. However, the role also depends heavily on trust-building, persuasion, negotiation, account strategy, and understanding messy customer environments, so AI is more likely to change workflows than fully remove the human role. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper technical sales support could let firms cover more accounts, customize more solutions, and sell to smaller customers, but customer buying cycles, budgets, and relationship constraints limit expansion. Because disruption is high but demand expansion is only moderate, the occupation is best categorized as restructure.
gpt56sol_rationale: AI can materially accelerate product research, requirements analysis, proposal and presentation creation, solution configuration, demonstrations, and routine technical support. However, complex discovery, negotiation, customer trust, and coordination around high-value implementations still require human judgment and interpersonal skill. Lower-cost sales engineering could expand coverage to smaller accounts and support a growing range of sophisticated products, but demand remains constrained by the volume of business purchases and customers’ appetite for sales engagement. The occupation therefore is likely to restructure around AI-enabled productivity, consultative selling, and oversight of automated technical workflows rather than disappear.
fable5_rationale: A large share of sales engineers' supporting work—preparing technical presentations, answering RFPs, product configuration, troubleshooting documentation, and market research—is digital and squarely in AI's path, but the core of the job remains high-stakes, trust-based persuasion, relationship building, and negotiation with enterprise buyers, which AI cannot replace. Elasticity is moderate: cheaper technical pre-sales support doesn't dramatically expand the number of complex B2B deals, though lower cost-of-sale could let vendors pursue more mid-market customers with dedicated technical selling. With disruption at 6, AI restructures the workflow (fewer hours on decks and documentation, more on customer-facing strategy) without displacing the relational core, making the occupation resilient. BLS's projected 5% growth is consistent with continued demand for humans who translate increasingly complex technology into buyer trust.
grok45_rationale: Core tasks such as preparing technical presentations, analyzing customer requirements, customizing recommendations, and generating support materials are predominantly knowledge- and language-based work where current AI tools already materially accelerate content creation, personalization, and data synthesis, though relationship-building, live persuasion, and negotiation still require human presence. If AI made the role 10x faster and cheaper, lower sales-process costs would unlock additional mid-market and complex-product deals that were previously uneconomical, producing meaningful but not unlimited demand expansion constrained by overall market size and sales-cycle realities. This combination of high disruption with moderate elasticity means the occupation persists but shifts substantially toward AI-fluent high-touch selling; workers who fail to adapt face displacement while those who master the new tools thrive.

title: Sales managers
claude_rationale: Sales managers face moderate disruption as AI can assist with data analysis, sales forecasting, CRM management, and performance tracking, but the core responsibilities of leadership, relationship building, strategic planning, and team management remain fundamentally human-centered. The role requires significant interpersonal skills, customer relationship management, and complex decision-making that AI cannot fully replicate. Demand elasticity is moderate - while AI-enhanced sales tools could make sales operations more efficient and potentially expand market reach, the need for sales managers is largely tied to organizational structure and team size rather than cost sensitivity. The net effect is resilient because despite meaningful AI assistance in analytical tasks, the core managerial and relationship-building aspects of the role remain largely intact.
opus_rationale: Sales managers perform significant data analysis, forecasting, and CRM work that AI tools already materially enhance, but the core of the role—leadership, motivating teams, building relationships, negotiating, and strategic judgment—relies on human interpersonal skills that AI cannot replace. This keeps disruption at the high end of moderate rather than fully high. Demand elasticity is moderate since cheaper sales analytics could let more organizations optimize sales strategy, but the management headcount is tied to team size and organizational structure rather than output volume. Because disruption stays at 6 (the periphery is automated but the leadership core remains human-centric), the occupation is resilient.
opus5_rationale: A large share of sales management work — pipeline and sales data analysis, forecasting, territory and quota design, budgeting, CRM hygiene, lead prioritization, training content, and performance reporting — is digital and language-based, and AI-enabled revenue-intelligence tools already automate much of it, though relationship-building, negotiation, hiring, and motivating human teams keep the role from being fully in AI's path. Demand for revenue generation is genuinely expansive (firms rarely say they want less selling), and cheaper sales capability can unlock more accounts, segments, and geographies being actively covered, but manager headcount is structurally tied to span-of-control over sales reps, and AI-driven self-service/automated selling could shrink the rep base that managers oversee, capping expansion at moderate. The mix of high task disruption and moderate demand elasticity means the occupation persists at roughly stable-to-slightly-growing headcount but with a substantially different skill set — from spreadsheet-driven reporting and coaching mechanics toward AI-tool orchestration, strategic account judgment, and interpreting model-generated forecasts. Managers who cannot move up the value chain from data wrangling to strategy and human leadership will be squeezed out.
openai_rationale: Sales managers' roles involve a mix of digital and interpersonal tasks, such as analyzing sales data and setting goals, which AI can assist with significantly. AI tools can enhance data analysis, customer relationship management, and sales forecasting, leading to a moderate level of disruption. However, the core tasks of leadership, strategy, and interpersonal communication still require human skills. On the elasticity side, as AI makes sales processes more efficient, the demand for sales management can expand, especially in sectors where sales strategies are crucial for competitiveness. This suggests a high elasticity, as businesses will likely invest more in sales management to leverage AI-driven insights, leading to an 'augment' net effect.
gpt55_rationale: Sales managers do substantial digital and cognitive work—CRM analysis, forecasting, territory planning, performance monitoring, customer segmentation, training design, and written communication—that AI can already accelerate significantly. However, the occupation also depends on leadership, motivation, hiring judgment, conflict resolution, customer relationship management, and accountability for revenue outcomes, which limits full automation. Demand is moderately elastic because cheaper sales analytics and coaching could help firms pursue more segments, channels, and customers, but managerial headcount is still constrained by organizational structure and spans of control. The result is restructuring: AI will change the skill mix and allow each manager to oversee more data-driven selling activity, but it is unlikely to eliminate the role broadly.
gpt56sol_rationale: AI can substantially automate sales forecasting, pipeline analysis, territory planning, reporting, training content, and performance monitoring, while also supporting customer outreach and complaint resolution. Human leadership, motivation, negotiation, accountability, and relationship management remain central, preventing near-total automation. Lower-cost analysis and coaching may let organizations pursue more customers and support larger sales operations, but each manager may also oversee more representatives, so demand expansion is only moderate. The role therefore persists but shifts toward strategic judgment, interpersonal leadership, and effective supervision of AI-enabled sales processes.
fable5_rationale: AI already materially assists the analytical portions of this job — sales forecasting, pipeline analysis, territory planning, quota setting, and CRM-driven reporting are squarely in AI's path. However, the core of the role is interpersonal: recruiting, coaching, and motivating sales reps, resolving escalated customer issues, and building relationships with dealers and distributors, which keeps disruption at the top of the moderate band rather than higher. Elasticity is moderate — headcount is largely tied to the size of sales teams and span of control rather than the cost of analysis, so faster analytics alone won't dramatically expand demand for managers, though cheaper sales operations may modestly grow sales organizations. With disruption at 6, the occupation is resilient: the analytical toolkit will shift substantially, but the leadership core keeps the role intact.
grok45_rationale: Sales managers' core work is predominantly knowledge-based—data analysis, forecasting, goal-setting, budgeting, strategy development, and training design—all of which AI tools already materially accelerate via CRM analytics, generative planning, and automated reporting, even while people-leadership and escalated interpersonal resolution remain human. Demand elasticity is only moderate because cheaper, faster sales management unlocks some expansion (more sophisticated strategies, broader market coverage, better support for growing sales forces) but is constrained by organizational structure, span-of-control norms, and the finite number of sales organizations; productivity gains therefore shift skill requirements more than they expand headcount. This combination of high disruption with moderate elasticity produces a restructured occupation in which adaptive managers thrive with AI leverage while others are displaced.

title: School and career counselors and advisors
claude_rationale: AI significantly disrupts the knowledge-work portions of counseling through tools that can analyze student data, match interests to careers, provide initial assessments, and offer 24/7 guidance, but the core human elements of empathy, relationship-building, and complex emotional support remain essential. Demand elasticity is high because AI-powered counseling tools could dramatically expand access to personalized guidance - currently many students receive limited counseling due to high counselor-to-student ratios, and cheaper AI-assisted counseling could serve underserved populations and provide more frequent, personalized support. The combination of moderate-to-high disruption with high elasticity suggests counselors will increasingly work alongside AI tools to serve many more students effectively.
opus_rationale: The disruption score is moderate because while assessments, data analysis, college/career information lookup, and résumé/interview prep are clearly AI-augmentable, the core of the job—building trusting relationships, providing emotional support, handling sensitive student issues like abuse/neglect, and navigating school systems with parents and teachers—requires human presence, compassion, and judgment that AI cannot replicate. The elasticity is moderate because cheaper guidance could expand access (more underserved students get personalized career/college advice), but school counselor headcount is largely determined by enrollment, budgets, and state mandates rather than productivity-driven demand. Because disruption stays at or below 6, the occupation is resilient: AI tools will handle informational and administrative tasks, freeing counselors to focus on the interpersonal and developmental work that defines the role.
opus5_rationale: A meaningful slice of this work is information-heavy and highly automatable — college/financial aid research, aptitude and interest matching, resume and interview coaching, course scheduling, data analysis of attendance and grades — and AI chatbots already handle much of the advising triage in higher education. But the core of school counseling is relational and situational: building trust with adolescents, crisis and behavioral intervention, mandated abuse reporting, family and teacher collaboration, and licensed presence in a physical school building, which caps disruption at the moderate-to-high boundary. Elasticity is high because counselor-to-student ratios are badly underserved (often 350-400:1 versus a recommended 250:1) and career coaching is a service most workers never access due to cost, so cheaper delivery unlocks large latent demand. Because the disruption score sits at 6 and the human, credentialed, in-person core remains intact, the occupation is resilient — AI reshapes the administrative and informational periphery while headcount continues its slow growth.
openai_rationale: The role of school and career counselors involves a mix of cognitive tasks such as data analysis and advising, alongside interpersonal tasks like counseling and collaboration, which are less susceptible to AI disruption. AI can assist in data analysis and administrative tasks, but the core human interaction and empathy required in counseling remain challenging for AI to replicate. Demand elasticity is moderate; while AI could make some aspects of counseling more efficient, the need for personalized guidance and support limits how much demand can expand. Thus, the occupation is resilient, with AI augmenting rather than replacing the core functions.
gpt55_rationale: AI can materially change many core tasks: interpreting assessments and student data, generating academic or career plans, answering college and financial-aid questions, helping with résumés and applications, and maintaining records. However, the occupation also depends heavily on trust, empathy, mandated reporting, crisis judgment, family and teacher coordination, and school-based presence, which limits full automation. Demand is moderately elastic because many students and workers are underserved and could use more personalized guidance if it were cheaper, but public school staffing, credentialing, budgets, and institutional ratios cap how much headcount expands. Because disruption is high but demand expansion is not strong enough to fully absorb productivity gains, the occupation is likely to be restructured around AI-enabled triage, advising tools, analytics, and higher-touch human counseling.
gpt56sol_rationale: AI can substantially automate career research, aptitude interpretation, academic planning, résumé support, recordkeeping, and identification of at-risk students. However, core school-counseling duties depend on trusted relationships, nuanced listening, crisis response, mandated reporting, and collaboration with families and staff, limiting end-to-end automation. Demand is highly latent because counseling caseloads are often large and personalized guidance is underprovided, although school budgets, credentialing, and institutional staffing constraints limit expansion. With disruption remaining just below the high-disruption threshold, AI is more likely to increase counselors’ capacity than fundamentally replace or restructure the occupation.
fable5_rationale: A meaningful portion of this work — career exploration, college matching, résumé and application help, aptitude assessment interpretation, and information delivery — is language-based and already well within AI's reach, which pushes disruption up. However, the core of school counseling involves in-person relationship-building, social-emotional support with minors, crisis intervention, mandated reporting, and collaboration with families and teachers, which anchors the human presence requirement and keeps disruption at the moderate-high boundary rather than above it. Elasticity is moderate: there is genuine latent demand (student-to-counselor ratios are far above recommended levels, and cheap career guidance would be consumed widely), but school budgets and staffing structures cap headcount expansion. With disruption at 6, the occupation lands in resilient — AI will absorb the informational advising tasks, but the interpersonal counseling core remains human work.
grok45_rationale: Core tasks center on interpersonal counseling, empathy-driven advising for social/behavioral issues, crisis response, and in-person collaboration with students, families, and staff—work that requires unpredictable human presence and trust—while AI only assists peripheral elements like data analysis of attendance/performance, aptitude matching, college/career information delivery, resume drafting, and record-keeping. This yields moderate disruption as AI tools already help knowledge portions but leave the relational core intact over the next decade. Elasticity is moderate because high student-to-counselor ratios and limited access to career coaching create some latent demand that cheaper/faster services could unlock (especially private career advising and expanded school programs), yet K-12 and higher-ed funding formulas, credentialing rules, and fixed student populations constrain dramatic expansion. With disruption at or below 6, the occupation remains resilient as AI augments edges without reshaping daily human-centered work.

title: Secretaries and administrative assistants
claude_rationale: Secretaries and administrative assistants perform predominantly digital, routine tasks like document preparation, scheduling, data entry, and email management that AI can already handle effectively. Current AI tools can automate most core functions including transcription, calendar management, basic document creation, and data organization. Demand for administrative support is relatively inelastic - organizations need a fixed amount of scheduling, filing, and basic correspondence regardless of cost, and productivity gains from AI will likely translate directly to fewer positions needed rather than expanded administrative services.
opus_rationale: Core tasks—document preparation, scheduling, email/memo writing, database management, transcription, and basic bookkeeping—are overwhelmingly digital and language-based, placing them directly in AI's path; modern tools already let managers and staff self-serve these functions, which BLS itself cites as a factor flattening employment. Demand is inelastic: organizations need a roughly fixed amount of administrative coordination, and cheaper/faster document handling does not cause businesses to consume dramatically more secretarial support—productivity gains translate into fewer support staff per manager rather than expanded output. With high disruption (8) and low elasticity (2), the occupation fits 'replace,' consistent with the flat-to-declining projections in most subcategories, with only medical secretaries partially insulated by healthcare-sector growth and physical/patient-facing tasks.
opus5_rationale: Core tasks — scheduling, drafting memos and reports, managing email and files, transcription, basic bookkeeping, and information lookup — are almost entirely digital, language-based, and highly routinized, placing them squarely in AI's direct path; agentic scheduling and document generation tools already absorb much of this work, though some in-person reception, physical mail, and interpersonal coordination remain. Demand is largely inelastic: administrative support is a fixed overhead function tied to headcount of the professionals being supported, not a service that organizations consume dramatically more of when it gets cheaper — instead, managers and clinicians increasingly self-serve. Medical secretaries are partly insulated by healthcare volume growth and insurance/patient-facing interaction, which is why BLS projects flat rather than steep decline. High disruption combined with low elasticity points to continued erosion of headcount and consolidation of remaining roles into fewer, higher-level coordinator positions.
openai_rationale: AI and digital tools are increasingly capable of handling the routine clerical and organizational tasks that secretaries and administrative assistants perform, such as scheduling, document preparation, and database management. This leads to a high disruption score as AI can automate many of these tasks. However, the demand elasticity is low because the core functions of secretaries and administrative assistants are not significantly suppressed by cost or speed; they are more about supporting existing workflows rather than generating new demand. Therefore, productivity gains from AI are likely to result in a reduced need for human workers, leading to a 'replace' net effect.
gpt55_rationale: Most core tasks for secretaries and administrative assistants are digital, routine, and language- or coordination-based: scheduling, drafting emails and memos, preparing documents, maintaining records, routing messages, and basic bookkeeping. AI assistants, workflow automation, transcription, document generation, and calendar tools already substitute for substantial portions of this work, though some roles still require interpersonal judgment, office presence, and domain-specific knowledge in medical, legal, or executive settings. Demand elasticity is low because organizations need administrative support roughly in proportion to their scale, managers, patients, or offices; making the work faster does not create a need for dramatically more scheduling or filing. Because disruption is high and demand expansion is limited, productivity gains are likely to reduce headcount or allow each assistant to support more people, fitting the replace category.
gpt56sol_rationale: Most core tasks—scheduling, correspondence, document preparation, transcription, record maintenance, and basic bookkeeping—are digital and increasingly automatable by AI agents integrated with office software. Human judgment, interpersonal coordination, and handling sensitive or specialized situations preserve some roles, especially in executive, medical, and legal settings. Demand has low elasticity because the amount of administrative support needed is largely determined by the number of executives, offices, patients, and transactions, while cheaper tools also enable other employees to perform these tasks themselves. High disruption combined with limited demand expansion makes replacement and substantial headcount consolidation the most likely net effect.
fable5_rationale: The core tasks — scheduling, drafting memos and emails, editing documents, transcription, managing calendars and databases, basic bookkeeping — are almost entirely digital, language-based work squarely in AI's current capabilities, and AI assistants already handle much of this today; only reception duties and in-person office coordination resist automation. Demand for administrative support is derived from organizational headcount, not suppressed by cost — making admin work 10x cheaper does not lead firms or executives to consume dramatically more of it, and the trend of managers self-serving with digital tools further caps demand. Some structural friction (healthcare front-office growth, personal-relationship value in executive roles) provides limited elasticity but not enough to absorb productivity gains. High disruption with low elasticity places this occupation firmly in the replace category, consistent with BLS projecting declines in three of four subcategories.
grok45_rationale: Core tasks—document drafting and editing, scheduling, email/phone handling, database maintenance, basic bookkeeping, and report preparation—are almost entirely digital, cognitive, and language-based, already being materially automated by generative AI, scheduling agents, and office software; physical or unpredictable real-world elements are peripheral. Demand for administrative support is largely a fixed cost of organizational activity rather than a service with large latent unmet need, so 10x productivity gains primarily allow managers and staff to self-serve or consolidate roles rather than expand total headcount. This combination of very high disruption and low elasticity produces net replacement pressure, consistent with BLS projections of flat-to-declining employment driven by technology.

title: Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents
claude_rationale: This occupation faces high disruption as core tasks like market analysis, trade execution, portfolio recommendations, and client research are increasingly automated through AI-powered trading systems, robo-advisors, and algorithmic analysis tools. The BLS already notes that automated trading systems have reduced demand for securities traders and simpler transactions can be completed online without brokers. However, demand elasticity is low because financial services consumption is relatively fixed - individuals and institutions don't dramatically increase their trading or investment advisory needs just because costs drop, and regulatory constraints limit market expansion. The combination of high AI disruption with constrained demand growth points to significant headcount contraction in this field.
opus_rationale: The core work — market analysis, trade execution, securities valuation, portfolio recommendations, and financial modeling — is almost entirely digital, cognitive, and quantitative, putting it directly in AI's path; algorithmic trading and robo-advisors have already displaced large portions of trading and simple brokerage work. Demand elasticity is low because the total volume of trades, IPOs, M&A deals, and assets under management is bounded by macroeconomic activity and heavy regulation rather than by the cost of advice, so cheaper execution does not meaningfully multiply transaction volume. The relationship-driven, high-touch sales and client-trust segment provides some buffer, but the bulk of analytical and transactional tasks face automation without offsetting demand growth, yielding net headcount pressure consistent with replace (disruption >=7, elasticity <=4).
opus5_rationale: The analytical and information-processing core of this work — market monitoring, security research, comparable-company and valuation analysis, pitch book and prospectus drafting, client prospecting lists, and algorithmic execution — is almost entirely digital and squarely in AI's path, and automation has already hollowed out floor trading and simple order execution. What limits the disruption score is that a large share of the job is relationship-building, persuasion, trust, and regulated fiduciary judgment with clients who want a human accountable for their money. Elasticity is moderate: cheaper advice does unlock some latent demand among mass-affluent and smaller-business clients who currently get no personalized service, but robo-advisory tools capture much of that segment without adding human headcount, and deal flow in IPOs and M&A is capped by capital-market cycles and regulation rather than by advisor cost. The result is restructuring: total employment roughly flat as commodity execution and research roles shrink while the surviving job shifts toward complex advisory, specialized expertise, and client relationship management augmented by AI analytics.
openai_rationale: AI is poised to significantly disrupt the securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents' occupation. Automated trading systems and AI-driven analytics are already transforming how trades are executed and how financial advice is given, reducing the need for human intervention in routine transactions. However, the demand elasticity is moderate because while AI can handle many transactions, the need for personalized financial advice and complex deal-making, such as IPOs and mergers, still requires human expertise. Demand elasticity is moderate because while AI could enhance productivity, the demand for special education is primarily driven by regulatory requirements and the specific needs of students, which are not significantly suppressed by cost. Thus, the occupation is resilient, with AI augmenting rather than replacing the human element.
gpt55_rationale: AI can substantially assist special education teachers with lesson adaptation, IEP drafting, progress documentation, assessment analysis, communication with parents, and assistive technologies for students. However, the core work still depends heavily on in-person instruction, behavioral support, emotional regulation, physical assistance, relationship-building, and legally accountable professional judgment. Demand has moderate elasticity because cheaper individualized supports could improve services and expand interventions, but headcount is constrained by school funding, enrollment levels, legal staffing models, and the need for adult supervision. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to displace the human-centered core of the occupation, the net effect is resilient.
gpt56sol_rationale: AI can substantially streamline IEP drafting, lesson adaptation, assessment analysis, progress documentation, and creation of personalized learning materials. However, the core work depends on in-person observation, relationship-building, behavioral support, safeguarding, and responsive instruction for students with diverse and sometimes severe disabilities. Cheaper personalization could improve service intensity and reach more underserved students, but enrollment, legal requirements, staffing ratios, and public-school budgets limit demand expansion. Because AI reshapes supporting knowledge tasks without replacing the human-centered core, the occupation is resilient.
fable5_rationale: AI can meaningfully assist with IEP drafting, lesson adaptation, progress tracking, and personalized learning materials, but the core work — in-person instruction, behavioral management, emotional support, and hands-on work with students who have physical, emotional, or severe cognitive disabilities — requires human presence and relationship-building that AI cannot replace. Elasticity is moderate: there is genuine unmet demand for special education services (chronic teacher shortages, caseload caps, earlier identification of disabilities), but growth is constrained by public school funding and enrollment rather than service cost. With disruption at 4, the occupation is resilient — AI will lighten the substantial paperwork burden (a major pain point) and could actually improve retention rather than reduce headcount.
grok45_rationale: Core duties center on in-person instruction, real-time behavioral and emotional support, physical assistance, and mentoring of students with disabilities—tasks that require human presence and adaptability AI cannot yet perform—while AI already assists knowledge-work elements such as IEP drafting, lesson adaptation, progress analytics, and record-keeping, producing moderate overall disruption. Demand is anchored to the relatively fixed population of identified students with disabilities and is constrained by federal funding mandates, school budgets, and enrollment trends, so productivity gains are unlikely to unlock large new volumes of service. Consequently AI will mainly streamline peripheral and administrative work without displacing the occupation’s essential human core, placing it in the resilient category.

title: Special effects artists and animators
claude_rationale: AI is highly disruptive to special effects and animation work, as generative AI tools can now create sophisticated 2D/3D models, animations, and visual effects that previously required extensive manual work. However, demand elasticity is high because cheaper, faster animation production unlocks massive latent demand across gaming, streaming content, social media, advertising, and emerging platforms like VR/AR. The cost barrier that previously limited animation to big-budget productions is rapidly falling, enabling more creators and businesses to incorporate high-quality visual content.
opus_rationale: The work is almost entirely digital and creative — modeling, animation, VFX, and image generation are squarely in the path of generative AI tools that can already produce images, video, and 3D assets. Demand elasticity is high because visual content production is heavily cost- and time-constrained; cheaper production unlocks far more games, films, mobile apps, ads, and personalized media as creators and small studios who couldn't previously afford polished VFX enter the market. Because disruption is high (8) and latent demand for visual content is large and price-sensitive (7), productivity gains are likely absorbed by expanded output rather than pure headcount cuts, though individual roles will shift toward AI-directed and supervisory creative work.
opus5_rationale: The work is almost entirely digital creation — modeling, animating, compositing, texturing, and even code — precisely the domain where generative image/video models, AI rotoscoping, motion capture cleanup, and procedural asset tools are already in production pipelines, so disruption is very high. Demand elasticity is high because animation and VFX are notoriously cost-constrained: studios cut shots, indie developers and small advertisers skip animation entirely, and long-form animated content is rationed by budget; if per-shot cost collapses, far more content gets animated across games, streaming, ads, social, and personalized media. Because 62% are self-employed freelancers serving a fragmented market, cheaper tools tend to expand the number of viable projects rather than consolidate headcount, though individual roles shift toward direction, art supervision, and AI-pipeline orchestration. Net effect is augment, with the caveat that mid-level production tasks (in-betweening, cleanup, basic asset creation) will contract sharply while creative-lead and technical-integration roles grow.
openai_rationale: Special effects artists and animators are highly susceptible to AI disruption due to the digital nature of their work. AI tools are already being used to automate parts of the animation process, such as generating realistic movements and effects. As AI continues to advance, it will increasingly assist in creating more complex animations and special effects. However, the demand elasticity is high because the entertainment industry is driven by consumer demand for more content and higher quality visual effects. As AI reduces costs and speeds up production, more projects can be undertaken, expanding the market for these skills. Thus, while AI will change how work is done, it will likely lead to an overall increase in demand for special effects and animation, resulting in an 'augment' net effect.
gpt55_rationale: This occupation is highly exposed because much of the core work is digital creation, editing, rendering, visual design, and iteration—areas where generative image, video, motion, and 3D tools are already materially changing workflows. Human artistic judgment, story coherence, client direction, and production-pipeline integration remain important, but many routine animation, effects, background, and concepting tasks are directly in AI’s path. Demand has moderate elasticity: cheaper animation and VFX will unlock more indie games, ads, social media content, educational media, and lower-budget productions, but audience attention, studio budgets, IP constraints, and quality-control needs limit unlimited expansion. The occupation therefore is likely to be restructured rather than simply replaced or broadly augmented, with fewer purely production-oriented roles and more emphasis on art direction, prompt/tool fluency, pipeline supervision, and creative integration.
gpt56sol_rationale: Animation and visual-effects production is almost entirely digital, and generative AI already accelerates concept art, modeling, rigging, in-betweening, compositing, and revision workflows. Human artistic direction, narrative judgment, consistency, and collaboration remain important, but the production pipeline and required technical skills will change substantially. Lower costs should unlock more animation and effects for games, advertising, independent media, mobile applications, and personalized content, although audience attention and major-studio budgets limit expansion. The high disruption combined with substantial latent demand makes augment the best fit, with workers producing far more output while routine production roles face pressure.
fable5_rationale: The work is almost entirely digital — modeling, rendering, compositing, and animating are directly in the path of generative image and video AI, which can already produce effects and animation that previously required teams of specialists, driving a very high disruption score. Elasticity is moderate: cheaper animation unlocks real latent demand (indie games, small-studio films, advertising, mobile content), but total consumption of visual media is capped by audience attention, and generative tools increasingly let directors and non-specialists produce effects without dedicated artists, so demand expansion won't fully absorb the productivity gains. The occupation will survive but shift dramatically toward AI-directed workflows, prompt-driven asset generation, and creative supervision rather than frame-by-frame craft. Artists who master AI pipelines can thrive on higher output; those relying on traditional technical execution face displacement, making restructure the fitting category.
grok45_rationale: Core work is almost entirely digital and generative—creating 2D/3D models, CGI, character animation, and VFX in software—so generative AI tools already produce usable assets, in-betweens, backgrounds, and even short sequences, placing the occupation firmly in AI’s direct path. Demand elasticity is high because lower cost and faster turnaround unlock substantial latent volume: more indie games, streaming content, mobile apps, advertising, educational media, and social video that were previously constrained by production budgets. Productivity gains therefore expand total output rather than simply shrinking headcount, allowing skilled artists who direct and refine AI systems to produce far more while overall employment remains stable or grows. This matches the augment category of high disruption paired with high elasticity.

title: Speech-language pathologists
claude_rationale: Speech-language pathology involves moderate disruption as AI can assist with assessment tools, documentation, and treatment planning, but the core work requires direct human interaction, physical examination of speech mechanisms, and personalized therapeutic relationships that AI cannot replicate. The elasticity is high because cheaper and more accessible speech therapy services could unlock significant latent demand - many people with communication disorders currently go untreated due to cost and availability constraints, and AI-assisted tools could make basic screening and supplementary therapy more widely available. However, since disruption remains moderate (5), this occupation falls into the resilient category where AI enhances rather than transforms the fundamental nature of the work.
opus_rationale: Core work involves hands-on assessment, hands-on therapy for speech/swallowing muscles, and compassionate face-to-face interaction with clients and families who are often children, stroke patients, or those with autism — these require human presence and cannot be automated. AI assists with documentation, diagnostic tool selection, progress tracking, and AAC technology, but the therapeutic core remains physically and interpersonally grounded, putting disruption in the moderate range. Demand elasticity is high because speech therapy is currently underserved (long waitlists in schools, aging population, growing autism awareness), so cheaper administrative overhead could unlock more treatment, but this doesn't change the headcount picture much. With disruption at or below 6, this occupation is resilient — AI touches the periphery (notes, scheduling, assessment tools) but does not reshape the hands-on clinical core.
opus5_rationale: Core work is in-person, relational therapy: eliciting speech, physically assessing swallowing, motivating frustrated clients and coaching families — tasks that require human presence, clinical judgment, and licensure. AI does meaningfully touch the periphery and some middle: documentation, IEP and progress-note drafting, automated speech/voice analysis, and AI-driven home practice apps that extend therapy between sessions, so disruption is moderate rather than low. Elasticity is high because speech therapy access is severely rationed by cost, waitlists, and clinician shortages in schools and rural areas — cheaper delivery would unlock large latent demand.
